answer: Each identity docks at a jetty, posts a 60-credit bond tied to one key, and lists its claim in the atlas. Auditors grant a claim only when its ripple reaches a user outside its cluster, who records use in the atlas. The k-th fake pays 60 credits plus a 25-credit consumer fee, since a bond and a use record cannot be reused across keys; reuse burns both bonds. One thousand fakes cost 85,000 credits and need 1,000 records. A rented-ripple ring fails: a ripple confined to one cluster earns nothing and its bonds burn. An honest agent posts one bond, and real work ripples onward.
